claims.claim: LECSEG-30 is a compact lecture benchmark with hierarchical labels.
claims.wording: 30 public lectures, 32.52 hours, 419 creator chapter boundaries, 904 reviewed subtopics, chapter kappa 0.5351.

claims.claim: Cross-model conservative selection significantly improves Pk/WD over BGE-divisive.
claims.wording: Pk improves from 0.3884 to 0.3713 (delta -0.0171, p=0.0064); WD improves from 0.3956 to 0.3764 (delta -0.0193, p=0.0001).

claims.claim: Balanced method selection gives the best deployable mean Pk/WD operating point.
claims.wording: Balanced selector reaches Pk=0.3588, WD=0.3739, BS=0.0757, F1@2=0.0893; its Pk/WD gains over cross-model are not significant.

claims.claim: Balanced selector significantly improves Pk/WD over BGE-divisive.
Balanced selector improves boundary-hit metrics over cross-model.
The selector result is sensitive to method-pool size.
claims.wording: Among tested balanced selector pools, k80 is best for Pk and WD; k120 worsens to Pk=0.3716, WD=0.3852.

claims.claim: Selector gains are not uniform across academic domains.
claims.wording: Selector improves Pk over BGE-divisive in 4/5 domains; failure domains: Math.

claims.claim: The selector is not domain-general under leave-one-domain-out evaluation.
claims.wording: Leave-domain-out selector drops to Pk=0.4012, WD=0.4103, worse than BGE-divisive and cross-model.

claims.claim: Candidate/method selection remains the main bottleneck.
claims.wording: Per-video oracle reaches Pk=0.2980, WD=0.3280; balanced selector switches on 30/30 videos but improves Pk over cross-model on only 9/30.

claims.claim: LECSEG should not be presented as universal external best system.
claims.wording: Large supervised chaptering systems use far more data; LECSEG's contribution is a reproducible low-resource lecture benchmark and analysis artifact.
